newsitem.title: USA: Kodak names new Consumer Imaging COOs.
newsitem.headline: Kodak names new Consumer Imaging COOs.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co named Henri Petit and Patrick Siewert as co-chief operating officers of its Consumer Imaging business, in an attempt to improve global focus and worldwide strategies, the company said Wednesday.

Analysts said the move is likely an effort to shake up Kodak's largest business following recent lackluster performance and concerns that it is on the losing end of a "price war" in the U.S. photo film market with its biggest rival Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd.
Current Consumer Imaging COO Alexander Wasilov will exchange positions with Siewert, and become head of the company's Greater China Region, Kodak said.
Stewart and Petit will report to David Biehn, president of Consumer Imaging. Petit currently heads the company's operations in its European, African and Middle Eastern Region.
"Petit and Siewert have excellent track records in driving results in the face of challenging business opportunities, said Daniel Carp, Kodak president and chief operating officer.

"Siewert's career responsibilities have taken him from the U.S. and Canada, to Europe and now China. He brings a unique global perspective to his new role. Petit combines his own international credentials with a record of business success. He understands traditional photography and digital imaging both as a technologist and general manager."
The company also said it named Charles Brown Jr as assistant general manager, Sensitized Goods Manufacturing.

"Wasilov and Brown have made significant contributions to Kodak's Consumer business, during a period in which we gained worldwide share and launched the best family of color films in the world," said Biehn.
